Render a camera path or data that change over time

Source: R/animate-3d.R
animate_3d.Rd

Render a scene from successive camera positions, or draw one subset of the data per frame. Projection, visibility and lighting are evaluated per frame.

Usage

animate_3d(
  plot,
  azimuth = NULL,
  elevation = NULL,
  zoom = NULL,
  frames = 60L,
  fps = 20,
  file = NULL,
  renderer = c("raster", "vector"),
  roll = NULL,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  antialias = 1L,
  progress = interactive(),
  time = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  workers = 1L,
  tween = NULL,
  trail = NULL,
  isometry = NULL,
  tour = NULL,
  stable_partition = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

azimuth, elevation, zoom, roll

A scalar, a numeric vector of length frames, or a function receiving times in seconds and returning either. NULL retains the plot setting, except azimuth without time or path, which makes one full turn.

frames

Number of frames, default 60. The closing view is excluded from the default turn so that looping repeats each view once. With time, one frame per distinct value of the time column. With path, the default samples the path at fps frames per second, and a given number of frames is spread evenly over the path.

fps

Frames per second, default 20.

file

Output path, or NULL to return PNG frame paths. The extension selects the output: .gif (needs gifski), .mp4 or .webm (need av), .apng (an animated PNG), .png or .svg (one file per frame; svg needs svglite) and .pdf (one page per frame). A file per frame takes its number from a sprintf() pattern in the name, such as "frames/turn-%03d.png", or else gets it appended, as in turn-0001.png. .glb and .gltf hold the first panel as an animated 3D scene for Blender and other glTF software: camera translation, rotation and zoom tracks, with per-frame visibility tracks for changing geometry. Each glTF animation uses one projection type; export perspective and orthographic paths separately.

renderer

Scene backend, "raster" (default) or "vector". Use "vector" for vector pages in SVG and PDF output.

width, height

Frame dimensions in pixels, default 640 each.

dpi

Device resolution, default 96 dots per inch. SVG and PDF pages measure width / dpi by height / dpi inches.

antialias

Raster supersampling factor, default 1.

progress

Report rendering time for each frame, default interactive().

time

Name of a data column holding the frame of each row, or NULL (default) for a fixed scene. Frame i draws the rows whose value equals the i-th sorted distinct value; layers without the column appear in every frame. Scales are trained on all frames, so limits, breaks and colour mappings are the same in each frame.

path

A camera path from camera_path_3d(), orbit_3d(), fly_through_3d() or dolly_zoom_3d(), or NULL. A path replaces azimuth, elevation, zoom and roll and also moves the target, distance, field of view and projection.

workers

Number of processes drawing frames, default 1, or a cluster from parallel::makeCluster() with ggplot3d loaded on its nodes. Each worker draws a contiguous run of frames on its own devices, so the frames are identical for every number of workers. Workers fork where the platform allows it and otherwise start socket processes, which load the installed ggplot3d. PDF pages are drawn in one process.

tween

A tween_3d() specification for in-between data frames, or NULL for one frame per state. Requires time. The number of frames is then (number of states - 1) * (tween$n + 1) + 1.

trail

NULL (default), a positive integer giving the number of preceding rendered frames in a motion trail, or a list with length and optional radius, width, sides (default 8), taper (default FALSE), normal and layers (layer indices). Trails follow the anchors of time-varying row-based marks, including points, text and solid glyphs. Map group to a persistent object identifier. Trails use geom_tube_3d()'s sweep; setting width selects a ribbon. Cross-section sizes use transformed position units; the default radius is 0.5% of the panel range diagonal. Mapped radius, width and twist are retained. Alpha fades linearly with frame age, multiplying the mark's alpha. taper = TRUE also scales the cross section by this fraction. Requires time; tweened frames count towards the window. Static layers stay fixed. Missing observations break a trail.

isometry

A list of one canonical-space isometry matrix per frame, a matrix shared by all frames, or a function of frame times returning the list. Re-emits geometry through the space adapter; an isometry that acts linearly on the display model (Lorentz transformations in the Klein model) changes only the camera pre-transform. Limits remain fixed.

tour

A tour_grand() specification or tourr history array. Applies Grassmann-interpolated bases to stat_project_3d() layers with orthographic or finite perspective projection. Uses fixed limits across frames. Requires static input data, linear position scales, and no tween or trail.

stable_partition

Cut overlapping faces on planes fixed by the geometry, default FALSE. Faces that occlude one another in a cycle must be cut before they can be painted back to front. By default each frame chooses its cuts from the view, so cut edges move between frames. With TRUE, the cuts come from one partition of the plot's faces and quadric surfaces by their own planes (Fuchs, Kedem and Naylor 1980), built once and reused while the geometry stays the same; each frame only walks it back to front for its camera. The drawn image is the same as without it; only the position of the cut edges differs. Quadric stand-ins are then refined for every viewing direction at the camera's distance and zoom. Applies to scenes the vector and hybrid renderers draw.

...

Arguments to export_3d() for glTF output: furniture, lines, points and size.

Value

A ggplot3d_animation list with file, frame_count, fps, camera (one row per frame with the time, the camera angles, zoom, projection, field of view, distance (NA when automatic) and target, and the frame's value of the time column when time is set), timings in seconds, transition (source state, destination state and eased fraction when tweening), build_seconds, frame, panel_extents in millimetres, and frames (the PNG paths when file is NULL, the written files of a per-frame output). PNG frames returned with file = NULL belong to the caller.

Details

Framing is "azimuth" when only the azimuth and zoom change, and "sphere" otherwise. Axis reserves and physical panel extents are fixed. Zoom remains an explicit magnification. Optional packages are checked before rendering. Rendering streams frames to disk. A fixed scene is built once; with time, each frame is built from its subset with the scale limits of the full data, as in gganimate's transition_manual() and plotly's frame aesthetic. The animated PNG follows the APNG 1.0 specification: browsers play it and viewers without APNG support show its first frame.

gganimate's transition_states() and transition_time() use a separate build pipeline. These transitions produce guidance to use animate_3d(time = , tween = tween_3d()) for a 3D plot.

See also

camera_path_3d() for keyframed camera moves, view_3d() to play a path in the browser.

Examples

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg, z = hp)) +
  geom_point_3d() + coord_3d()
if (requireNamespace("gifski", quietly = TRUE)) {
  movie <- animate_3d(p, frames = 3, width = 320, height = 320,
                      file = tempfile(fileext = ".gif"))
  movie$timings
}
if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  turn <- animate_3d(p, path = orbit_3d(degrees = 90, duration = 1), fps = 3,
                     width = 240, height = 240, file = tempfile(fileext = ".apng"))
  turn$camera$azimuth
}
waves <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 20), y = seq(0, 1, length.out = 20),
                     t = seq(0, 0.75, by = 0.25))
waves$z <- sin(pi * waves$x) * sin(pi * waves$y) * cos(2 * pi * waves$t)
wave <- ggplot2::ggplot(waves, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d() + coord_3d()
if (requireNamespace("gifski", quietly = TRUE)) {
  movie <- animate_3d(wave, time = "t", width = 320, height = 320,
                      file = tempfile(fileext = ".gif"))
  movie$camera$value
}
track <- data.frame(x = c(0, 1, 2), y = c(0, 1, 0), z = c(0, 0.5, 1), t = 1:3)
moving <- ggplot2::ggplot(track, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z, group = 1)) +
  geom_point_3d(colour = "steelblue", size = 3) + coord_3d()
if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) {
  wake <- animate_3d(moving, time = "t", tween = tween_3d(n = 1),
    trail = list(length = 3, radius = 0.04, taper = TRUE),
    width = 240, height = 240, progress = FALSE)
  unlink(wake$frames)
}
